newsitem.title: USA: IDC sees U.S. PC shipments up 13 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: IDC sees U.S. PC shipments up 13 pct in 1997.

text.p: International Data Corp said in its initial forecast for 1997 that it expects the U.S. personal computer industry to ship 13 percent more units next year than in 1996.
IDC also said it sees U.S. PC shipments for the current year growing 16.6 percent over 1995.
Eric Lewis, an IDC manager, said the 1996 forecast had been trimmed from around 16.9 percent, previously.
Lewis said Intel Corp's announcement this week that revenues would rise at least five percent sequentially in the third quarter confirmed IDC's growth projections.
"To me, it's confirmed we've been right all along, saying its a pretty good year," Lewis said.
"Last year was a boom year. This isn't a boom year," he said.

He noted the current growth rate is below last year's rate of 23 percent and he said going forward he sees higher saturation levels in the big business market and less growth in the consumer market than in the past.
